Produced by veteran Patricia Cheng and developed through Hong Kong’s First Feature Film Initiative, the 96-minute Cantonese production had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival.
The concept originated from a viral Hong Kong CCTV clip showing two people getting into an increasingly violent confrontation after a trivial physical collision. Yeung was less interested in the absurdity of the incident than in what might have brought two ordinary people to the point where something so insignificant could cause them to explode. His answer is a contemporary Hong Kong where financial pressure, work, family obligations and accumulated frustration constantly push people toward a tipping point.

ceramic.title: Films I watch repeatedly (a new series): His Girl Friday
ceramic.snippet: Skip to main content Labels Films I watch repeatedly (a new series):  His Girl Friday  After awhile, it feels like therapy. I get out  His Girl Friday (1940) or  Out of the Past (1947) and watch it for some sort of undefined solace. Joseph Epstein's new book entitled  Charm  discusses how one can look for the movies of the 1930s and 40s for exemplars of charm, and how Cary Grant could be one on film, but not necessarily one in person (only, it seems, Audrey Hepburn could do that). The cast and crew of "We Are Born Good" pose together after winning Best Narrative Feature. CNA photo Nov. 22, 2026

Taipei, Nov. 22 (CNA) "We Are Born Good" (善男信女) won best narrative feature at the 63rd Golden Horse Awards on Sunday, taking home two awards at the ceremony held at the Taipei Music Center.

Directed by Yeung Leung-chuen (楊兩全), the film won over "Girl" (女孩), "Double Happiness" (雙囍), "Arrested Memory" (狂忘警探) and "We Are All Strangers" (我們不是陌生人) in the best narrative feature category.

Accepting the award, the Hong Kong director commented on how heavy the trophy was.

"But I feel I can lift it because everyone was truly wonderful," Yeung said.

He also urged people to go to the movies, saying films needed audiences.

"We Are Born Good" follows two people in Hong Kong: a man trying to rebuild his life by running a café after leaving prison, and a young woman trying to make a living while auditioning for acting roles.

When a food order goes wrong, the two blame each other, turning a minor dispute into a feud.

The film entered the ceremony with nine nominations and also won best original screenplay for Yeung and co-writer Thomas (火車).

Yeung Leung-chuen (right) and Thomas (left) win Best Original Screenplay together for "We Are Born Good."
